page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v5 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an ARM64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores utilizing the Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 1229 GB local SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. The hypervisor layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 57203.87 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12912.0. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1125.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1822.59. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only small block cached speed of 2232.35 GB/sec, which drops to 166.64 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database operations perform in the average range, with Redis SET operations reaching 40.63 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 21065.71.

The instance exhibits clear performance tradeoffs. While it handles multi-threaded tasks like bzip3 decompression and software compilation with average efficiency, it struggles with heavy computational workloads. Large language model inference speeds are poor, yielding only 3.6 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 70B model. Qualitatively, the ARM-based architecture provides a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high physical core density and local SSD storage without the premium cost of x86 architectures. This server is suitable for general-purpose workloads, web serving, software compilation, and database operations.
